claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions.

Let's start with the basics:

**Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you enquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I have one child I'm asking about. Their name is Alex and they're 17 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Since Alex is 17 years old, I need to ask you some important questions about their circumstances.

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training?** (For example, are they in school, college, sixth form, or an approved training program?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex is still in education. They're doing their A-levels at sixth form college.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's great, thank you. Now I need to understand your relationship with Alex and your living situation.

**Do you live with Alex in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives at home with me here in the UK. We're in Manchester.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent, thank you. Now I need to understand a bit more about your residency status to ensure you meet all the eligibility criteria.

**What is your immigration/residency status in the UK?** (For example, are you a British citizen, do you have settled status, pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme, or another status?)

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you for providing that information. Just one final question to complete my assessment:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?** (For example, Alex's other parent or another person?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Good news! You are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Based on the information you've provided:

✓ Alex is 17 years old and in approved education (A-levels at sixth form)
✓ You live with Alex in the UK
✓ You are a British citizen
✓ You are responsible for Alex
✓ No one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex

Since Alex is under 20 and remains in approved education, you qualify for Child Benefit even though they're over 16.

**Important things to remember:**
- You'll continue to receive Child Benefit as long as Alex stays in approved education or training and is under 20
- If Alex leaves education, starts working 24+ hours per week, starts an apprenticeship, or claims certain benefits in their own right, your Child Benefit may stop
- If you or your partner have an individual income over £60,000, you may need to pay the High Income Child Benefit tax charge

If you haven't already claimed, you can apply for Child Benefit. If your circumstances change, make sure to notify HMRC.
